Posted November 26, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
The Battle for Canada: Two Months to Defend Ourselves Against Prohibitionist Counterattack. Special Programs for Pot-TV and Documentation on MarijuanaNews.

On October 31, The Globe and Mail reported that the parliamentary committee examining Canada's proposed law to decriminalize possession of small amounts of marijuana is inviting one of the bill's chief critics -- U.S. drug czar John Walters -- to testify at its hearings.

Committee chair Paddy Torsney was quoted as saying, " We are open to listening to anybody give good advice to us. "

However, on November 4th, The Ottawa Citizen reported that Walters, and several other Americans, had declined to testify.

According to The Citizen, Tom Riley, Mr. Walter's public affairs spokesman, said his boss has been clear about what he thinks of Canada's proposed law so he sees no need to come north once again to repeat his position.

This obviously means that Walters position is unchanged and the Canadian Parliament should refer to the public record. As a service to the Parliament, I have assembled a series of quotes from Walters, which can thus be taken as what he would have said, had he deigned to come. (Wherever possible, I have provided links to the articles from which the quotes are taken.)

Thus, based on the public record, we have what we must assume would have been Walters testimony to the Canadian parliamentary committee hearings on cannabis legislation. Now what are the facts?
